fixed.text: A concern, two sayings parting, each carried by observings. One side: a chemically driven motor's direction, stopping force and greatest efficiency go with free-energy drops between its mechanical states, a power stroke; F1's ATP binding, about 10 kcal/mol, goes with an 80–90° substep, its single-molecule acceleration and deceleration phases parting from rotational diffusion, and myosin V shows a power stroke and then a constrained diffusive search. Its other side: direction and stopping force go with kinetic asymmetry alone, the relative barrier heights of chemical steps in different mechanical states, and two synthetic molecules with no designed power stroke turn with net direction under fuel at ensemble level. Not yet observed directly: fits to kinesin back-stepping data at q⁻¹ = 221 with 2.9 nm and q⁻¹ = 802 with 3.7 nm, for the second side; and, for the first, about 10 k_BT stored elastically at about 1.3° of bending or 2.3% strain, near thermal fluctuation, a steric push in an elastic one's place. Both sides fit one coarse single-molecule record, each with its own criterion for a power stroke, and light-driven and externally modulated motors go with a power stroke on both.
